All original text is present, with zero-based original span markers <SPAN i>...</SPAN i>. For supported/opposed hypotheses cite all original evidence span indices for that decision, including independently operative redundant support and necessary governing language. For NotMentioned return an empty evidence list. Treat conditions and exceptions within scope, and distinguish limited permission from universal permission. Give a short public reason (at most 15 words per hypothesis), then report supplied skill IDs actually used. Skills are fallible reusable inspection procedures, not facts about this NDA or automatic verdicts. All skills are visible together; public hypothesis IDs describe applicability, not hidden context isolation. Do not execute further tools, invent citations or rewrite span indices. Return exactly the supplied JSON schema with all 17 original hypothesis keys. For each emit choice, spans, reason, used_skill_ids in that order. The common schema describes permitted values, not answers about this contract. Evidence candidates are fallible, not mandatory citations; make every final label and evidence decision yourself from the complete original contract. Work through the supplied public hypotheses. Each question contains its own complete applicable skill records and fallible source candidates. All 17 questions and the full contract remain visible together; a skill on a different question is not a condition that this question must satisfy. Independently inspect the entire source even when this question has no skills or candidates. A missing skill, an unestablished when condition, or a null relation_if_established never means NotMentioned. A non-null conditional relation is not a verdict about this contract. Check the complete condition and original hypothesis polarity yourself. Skill IDs reported for a question must come from that question's supplied records; an empty used_skill_ids list is always allowed. Possible list introductions are fallible layout suggestions, not proven legal dependencies or required citations. Decide every original label and final evidence set yourself.

{"full_contract_with_original_span_markers":"<SPAN 0>NON – DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT</SPAN 0>
<SPAN 1> </SPAN 1><SPAN 2>This agreement made this __________ day of ___________ , 20__, by and between:______________________, (“Writer”), and __________________ (“Producer’), .</SPAN 2>
<SPAN 3>Whereas, Writer has written a script (“Submission”) for a possible future theatrical or motion picture production.</SPAN 3>
<SPAN 4> </SPAN 4><SPAN 5>Whereas, Writer wishes Producer to evaluate said “Submission” for the sole purpose of determining whether said Submission may be further developed into a motion picture (“Project”).</SPAN 5>
<SPAN 6>NOW, THEREAFTER, in consideration of the premises and mutual covenants herein contained, the parties agree as follows:</SPAN 6>
<SPAN 7>1. 1. </SPAN 7><SPAN 8>All information disclosed by Writer to Producer, in writing, whether or not such information is also disclosed orally, that relates or refers, directly or indirectly, to the Submission, including the Submission itself, shall be deemed confidential and shall constitute Confidential Information, and shall include </SPAN 8><SPAN 9>(i) all documents generated by Producer which contain, comment upon, or relate in any way to any Confidential Information received form Writer, and </SPAN 9><SPAN 10>(ii) any written samples of the Submission received from Writer together with any information derived by Producer there from. </SPAN 10><SPAN 11>.2. Confidential Information shall not include any information:</SPAN 11>
<SPAN 12> </SPAN 12><SPAN 13>.</SPAN 13><SPAN 14>(i) That Producer can show by documentary evidence was known to Producer or prior to the date of its disclosure to Producer by Writer or</SPAN 14>
<SPAN 15> </SPAN 15><SPAN 16>.</SPAN 16><SPAN 17>(ii) That becomes publicly known, by publication or otherwise, not due to any unauthorized act or omission of Producer or any other party having an obligation of confidentiality to Writer; or,</SPAN 17>
<SPAN 18> </SPAN 18><SPAN 19>.</SPAN 19><SPAN 20>(iii) That is subsequently disclos3ed by Writer to any person, firm or corporation on a on-confidential basis; or</SPAN 20>
<SPAN 21> </SPAN 21><SPAN 22>.</SPAN 22><SPAN 23>(iv) That producer can conclusively show by documentary evidence that such information was developed independent of any access to the Confidential Information.</SPAN 23>
<SPAN 24>2. 3. </SPAN 24><SPAN 25>Writer will disclose the Confidential Information to Producer solely for the purpose of allowing Producer to evaluate the Submission to determine, in its sole discretion, whether the Submission may be further developed into a Project.</SPAN 25>
<SPAN 26>3. 4. </SPAN 26><SPAN 27>Producer agrees to accept disclosure of the Confidential Information and to exercise the same degree of care to maintain the Confidential Information secret and confidential as is employed by Producer to preserve and safeguard its own materials and confidential information.</SPAN 27>
<SPAN 28>4. 5. </SPAN 28><SPAN 29>The Confidential Information shall remain the property of Writer and shall not be disclosed or revealed by Producer or anyone else except employees of Producer who have a need to know the information in connection with Producer’s evaluation of the Submission, and who have entered into a secrecy agreement with Producer under which such employees are required to keep confidential the Confidential Information of Writer, and such employees shall be advised by Producer of the confidential nature of the information and that the information shall be treated accordingly. </SPAN 29><SPAN 30>Producer shall be liable for any improper disclosure of the Confidential Information by its employees.</SPAN 30>
<SPAN 31> </SPAN 31><SPAN 32>.6. </SPAN 32><SPAN 33>(i) Producer shall notify Writer of any determination it may arrive at with respect to the further development of the submission, provided, however, that, in doing so, Producer shall not directly or indirectly disclose any Confidential Information to any third party, without the consent of Writer. </SPAN 33><SPAN 34>.</SPAN 34><SPAN 35>(ii) If Producer determines that the Submission cannot be further developed into a Project, within <….> months of the receipt of the Submission, Producer shall within five (5) business days after such determination return any and all Confidential Information to Writer, along with all copies or derivatives thereof and all writings generated by Producer in connection with Producer’s evaluation of the Submission or the Confidential Information.</SPAN 35>
<SPAN 36>5. 7. </SPAN 36><SPAN 37>If Producer determines that the Submission is suitable for further development into a Project, Producer and Writer will attempt to agree on a schedule for development, and compensation to Writer for the submission.</SPAN 37>
<SPAN 38>6. 8. </SPAN 38><SPAN 39>Other than as specifically provided herein, Producer will not use the Confidential Information for any purpose whatsoever other than for the sole purpose permitted in paragraph 3 hereof, unless and until a further executed agreement is first made between the parties setting forth the terms and conditions under which rights to the Submission and the Confidential Information are to be licensed to, or acquired by, Producer.</SPAN 39>
<SPAN 40>7. 9. </SPAN 40><SPAN 41>Writer agrees that it will not contact any party or parties other than Producer concerning the Confidential Information without prior written authorization from Producer during the term of this agreement.</SPAN 41>
<SPAN 42> </SPAN 42><SPAN 43>.10. Producer’s obligations under paragraphs 3,4, and 8 of this agreement shall extend from the date of this agreement and shall survive the expiration or termination of this agreement, provided, however, that Producer’s obligations under paragraphs 3 and 4 of this agreement shall terminate immediately in the event that Writer .shall purposefully disclose the Confidential Information to any other person, firm, or corporation on a non-confidential basis, during the term of this Agreement.</SPAN 43>
<SPAN 44>8. 11. </SPAN 44><SPAN 45>Writer hereby expressly warrants that it has the full right and authority to disclose the Confidential Information to Producer, and that no prior public non-confidential disclosure of the Confidential Information ahs been made by Writer nor, to the best of Writer’s knowledge, by any other party.</SPAN 45>
<SPAN 46>9. 12. </SPAN 46><SPAN 47>Nothing in this agreement shall be deemed a sale or offer for sale of the Submission, and nothing contained herein shall in any way obligate Writer to grant to Producer a license or any other rights, directly or by implication, estoppel or otherwise to the Confidential Information or the Submission.</SPAN 47>
<SPAN 48>10. 13. </SPAN 48><SPAN 49>Subject to paragraph 10 above, this agreement shall terminate ________ years from the date of this agreement, unless extended by mutual agreement of the parties. </SPAN 49><SPAN 50>This agreement may be terminated prior to the expiration of __________ from the date this agreement by either Writer or Producer upon thirty (30) days’ written notice to the other parties of an intention to terminate.</SPAN 50>
<SPAN 51>11. 14. </SPAN 51><SPAN 52>This agreement sets forth the entire agreement between the parties and may not be amended or modified except by a writing signed by all of the parties.</SPAN 52>
<SPAN 53>12. 15. </SPAN 53><SPAN 54>This agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.</SPAN 54>
<SPAN 55>13. 16. </SPAN 55><SPAN 56>This agreement may be executed in counterparts.</SPAN 56>
<SPAN 57>IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this agreement as of the day and year first above written.</SPAN 57>

<SPAN 59>By: By:</SPAN 59>

<SPAN 62>Date: Date:</SPAN 62>

guidance.when: Assessing whether return or destruction is required when the agreement or protected evaluation ends.
guidance.inspection: Identify both the required act and its trigger. Termination or expiration qualifies, as does an expressly stated conclusion, rejection, or abandonment of the evaluation or business possibility. A request-only duty or a party's mere decision not to proceed does not qualify without language making an end event itself the trigger.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative return-or-destruction duty and the language establishing its end-event trigger. Include every independent termination-triggered return or deletion obligation relied upon.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exception to a return or destruction obligation.
guidance.inspection: Check whether the exception expressly permits continued possession of backups, archival material, a legal copy, or another defined subset after the return/destruction event. Conditions on access, purpose, or continuing confidentiality do not negate the permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the retention exception and, when separated, the governing return/destruction clause showing the temporal context.

guidance.when: The agreement requires return or destruction of confidential information and copies without stating a retention exception.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether the duty is exhaustive as to the covered material and copies. A complete return/destruction command that leaves no authorized retained subset negates permission to possess some material afterward.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the exhaustive operative duty and verify across the complete agreement that no backup, archival, legal-copy, or other retention exception qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses ownership, licenses, or rights in confidential information or associated intellectual property.
guidance.inspection: Look for language that no license or right is granted, conveyed, conferred, or implied. A limited authorization to review or use information for the stated transaction does not by itself contradict the broader no-grant proposition.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the express no-grant clause; include an ownership clause only when it helps establish the object of the denied rights.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts disclosure of negotiations, discussions, a contemplated transaction, the agreement itself, or the existence of dealings.
guidance.inspection: A prohibition on revealing that negotiations or discussions exist establishes the hypothesis. A prohibition on public announcements concerning the agreement or transaction also qualifies; definition text alone must be paired with an operative nondisclosure duty.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative prohibition and the protected fact, retaining any governing introduction needed to connect a listed fact to the prohibition.

guidance.when: Confidential-information coverage is conditioned on marking, designation, or identification by the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that the identification condition grammatically governs every covered disclosure mode. A single terminal condition may govern an enumeration of oral, written, and electronic modes; different procedures may also govern different modes. Do not treat nature- or circumstances-based coverage as identification.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete definition or all clauses needed to show that every disclosure mode is subject to identification by the disclosing party.

guidance.when: The definition covers information either expressly designated confidential or reasonably understood to be confidential from its nature or disclosure circumstances.
guidance.inspection: The contextual alternative independently covers undesignated information, so express identification by the disclosing party is not required for all confidential information.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete alternative definition showing both designation and circumstance- or nature-based coverage.

guidance.when: Assessing whether the receiving party may make a copy in some circumstance.
guidance.inspection: Require an affirmative operational copying route, such as copies necessary for authorized use or acknowledged automatic backups. A prohibition phrased as applying without prior consent or approval is not by itself an affirmative permission to copy.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite language affirmatively authorizing, requiring, or acknowledging copy creation and its governing condition; disclosure or access permission is insufficient.

guidance.when: The agreement prohibits copying confidential information and contains no affirmative operational copying route.
guidance.inspection: A direct copy ban, including a ban stated as applying without prior consent or approval, negates the benchmark permission hypothesis when the complete agreement does not otherwise authorize necessary copies, backups, or another copying circumstance. Do not convert the consent qualifier itself into affirmative permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the copy prohibition and verify across the agreement that no affirmative operational-copy or backup route qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement permits disclosure to representatives or other persons.
guidance.inspection: Resolve who falls within the permitted class. Consultants, agents, counsel, accountants, professional advisers, affiliates, and similar non-employees establish sharing with some third parties; an employee-only exception does not.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the permission and the definition or enumeration proving that at least one permitted recipient is a third party, plus any need-to-know or confidentiality condition governing the permission.

guidance.when: The agreement states an authorized transaction, project, evaluation, business relationship, or other defined purpose for confidential information.
guidance.inspection: A command to use confidential information only for that purpose, or not for any other purpose, directly imposes the limited-use obligation. The existence of the authorized purpose is not a contradiction.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative use restriction and enough purpose language to identify the authorized scope.

guidance.when: Relevant candidate text is a numbered item, exception, continuation, anaphoric clause, or otherwise incomplete fragment.
guidance.inspection: Read the governing introduction and adjacent items to determine the item's legal function, trigger, subject, and exceptions. Keep independent operative clauses separately; do not treat a neighboring item as evidence merely because it shares the list.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include every span necessary to make the relied-on proposition complete, while excluding sibling items that do not establish that proposition.

guidance.when: The confidential-information definition enumerates subject matter or data categories.
guidance.inspection: Find an expressly covered non-technical category, such as business, financial, marketing, personnel, customer, contact, or transaction information. Generic references to all information, documents, analyses, form, or derivatives do not alone prove non-technical coverage.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the definition and at least one explicit non-technical category; include continuation text when the category list crosses fragments.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exclusion, reservation, or acknowledgment concerning independent development.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that the receiving party may develop information independently without using or accessing the protected information. Prior approval to disclose, lawful receipt, or another unrelated exception does not establish independent development.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the independent-development clause with its governing exclusion or reservation language when needed to make its legal function complete.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses information obtained from an external source or made available non-confidentially.
guidance.inspection: Look for lawful receipt from a source other than the disclosing party that is not bound by confidentiality, or for the disclosing party's later non-confidential release making the information externally available. Independent development and consent to the receiver's own disclosure are different matters.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the external-source or non-confidential-release clause and its governing exclusion introduction, including any condition concerning the source's authority or confidentiality duties.

guidance.when: The definition or coverage clause addresses communication form.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether oral or verbal communication is expressly within confidential information, including language covering information irrespective of communication form or information disclosed in writing and also orally. Do not infer oral coverage merely from derivative notes or documents.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the language linking oral, verbal, or form-independent communication to confidential-information coverage, with any necessary definition continuation.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts recruiting, hiring, employment contact, or solicitation involving personnel of the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Find a prohibition on soliciting, employing, hiring, or initiating employment contact with officers, employees, or other personnel. Proxy solicitation, transaction standstill language, and general contact restrictions are not personnel nonsolicitation unless tied to employment or hiring.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative employment-related prohibition and the covered personnel class; include duration, targeting limits, or recruiting exceptions when they qualify the prohibition.

guidance.when: The agreement states that duties continue beyond an end event or remain effective for a post-event period.
guidance.inspection: Verify that confidentiality, non-use, or another agreement obligation continues after termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, or an equivalent end of the protected relationship. Continuation merely after return or destruction does not establish survival of agreement termination.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the continuing obligation and the termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, or equivalent end event to which continuation is linked.
